input_packet.case_brief:
Solo founder deciding whether to pivot B2B SaaS product from current offering to new workflow tool amid flat growth, $4K MRR, 14 months runway, and 22 customers.

Constraints stated during conversation:
- [ACTIVE] Runway 14 months at current burn
- [ACTIVE] 22 paying customers on current product
- [ACTIVE] Two full-time employees (engineer, CS)
- [ACTIVE] Conversational signal from three customers, no commitments
- [ACTIVE] Former co-founder holds 15% equity, passive

Original framing: Founder assumes pivot signal from three customers is valid; weighs pivoting now with 14 months runway vs pushing current flat product; excludes other options beyond these two.
input_packet.anchor_visible_candidate:
SYNTHESIZED POSITION:
Run pre-buy test this week with the three customers at specific price ($X, 3 months prepay); define pass bar upfront (e.g., 2/3 commit); set decision in 14 days; if pass, pivot with transition plan for current customers (freeze/sunset/migrate), inform/talk to CS employee about uncertainty then likely layoff with severance, inform former co-founder without seeking input; have hard conversations first as they unlock the decision.
input_packet.deck_pressure_candidate: Before pivoting, convert the three customer signals into a pre-buy test with a named price, three-month prepay, and a written pass/fail bar. Keep fairness to the passive co-founder separate from decision rights: tell her the plan, but do not treat courtesy as veto power. Check competitive dynamics and migration cost before declaring the new workflow the company.

step6_output.answer_core:
This week, convert the three customer signals into a pre-buy test: offer the new workflow tool at a named price with a 3-month prepay commitment, and set a written pass/fail bar upfront (e.g., 2 of 3 commit). In parallel, run a quick check on competitive dynamics and migration cost from the current product so you do not declare the new workflow the company before mapping the switch economics. Set a hard decision deadline of 14 days.

Have the hard conversations first because they unlock the decision: tell your CS employee now about the uncertainty and the likely outcome—if you pivot, the role will end with severance—and inform your former co-founder (15%, passive) of the test and your intent to decide, without treating courtesy as veto power.

If the test hits the pass bar and the competitive/migration map is acceptable, pivot with a concrete transition plan for your 22 current customers (freeze, sunset, or migrate) and execute the CS transition. If it fails, preserve runway and optionality without drifting in an ambiguous middle.

private_visibility_ledger.why: The anchor provides the core architecture: the pre-buy test design (named price, 3-month prepay, written pass/fail bar), the 14-day decision window, the transition plan for 22 current customers, the hard-conversations-first sequencing, and the specific actor handling (CS layoff with severance, co-founder inform-only).
private_visibility_ledger.visible_effect: Public answer follows the anchor's structure, test mechanics, actor sequence, and named resources.

private_visibility_ledger.why: The competitive dynamics and migration cost check is a concrete, non-obvious validation step that prevents trading a flat product for a more expensive pivot. The co-founder fairness framing reinforces the anchor's instruction but the competitive/migration element is the distinct additive payload that changes the public answer structurally.
private_visibility_ledger.visible_effect: Inserts an explicit pre-declaration validation step (competitive dynamics + migration cost mapping) between the pre-buy test and full pivot commitment, and sharpens the co-founder communication to an inform-only stance.

added_entities: pre-declaration validation before new workflow becomes the company
reframed_emphasis: Co-founder communication framed as informing without granting veto power, reinforcing decision rights
structural_delta: Added stop condition: verify competitive dynamics and migration cost after pre-buy test pass but before declaring the new workflow the company
